result.summary: Nora (the tenant) has ruled out loose items in the drum. The washing machine clicking is a mechanical fault. The landlord hasn't approved anything on the records, so I emailed them asking to approve an engineer to inspect and quote. I followed lesson #36. I replied to Nora to say yes to her video offer and explain what happens next, and put the ticket on hold until the landlord answers, with a follow-up in 3 days.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 003 told Nora an engineer would be sent if nothing was stuck in the drum. Event 006 meets that condition: she reports a mechanical clicking noise and offers a video. Event 003 also says 'I have let the landlord know', but no approval is recorded, the landlord's profile has no spend limit, and there is no landlord reply. So I can't assign a contractor yet. Lesson #36 (troubleshooting ruled out, then ask the landlord to approve an inspection, reply to the tenant, hold) fits. Lesson #17 only applies when the landlord has already pre-approved, which they haven't here. The fault is routine: the machine still works and Jev rates it routine at 0.99.

alternatives_considered.why_not: No landlord approval or pre-approved limit is recorded; telling the landlord about the fault is not the same as approving it.

alternatives_considered.option: No reply to tenant / return to auto
alternatives_considered.why_not: Nora offered a video and is waiting to hear what happens next, so she needed a short reply.
Nothing conflicting and no safety risk; the normal next step is clear.
